newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-SMITH GETS 22-MONTH BAN FOR TAKING COCAINE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SMITH GETS 22-MONTH BAN FOR TAKING COCAINE.

text.p: Former Warwickshire all-rounder Paul Smith was on Tuesday banned from professional cricket for 22 months for taking cocaine.
Smith appeared before the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) disciplinary committee and was found guilty of taking an illegal substance while playing as a county cricketer.
After a hearing lasting a little more than an hour, Smith was banned from all cricket under ECB auspices until April 1 1999.
Smith, 33, left Warwickshire last summer after a 15-year career in which he played 221 games, scoring 8,173 runs and taking 283 wickets.
"I had a very fair hearing, that's not to say that I didn't find the verdict harsh," Smith said.
"There is a lesson to be learned from all this and the true story will come out."

The last cricketer to be suspended for drug taking, former Sussex fast bowler Ed Giddins, is currently serving a 20-month ban, at the end of which he will be qualified for Smith's former county Warwickshire.
